title: Migration, Climate Similarity, and the Consequences of Climate Mismatch
abstract: This paper introduces the concept of "climate matching" as a driver of migration and establishes several new results. First, we show that climate strongly predicts the spatial distribution of immigrants in the US, both historically (1880) and more recently (2015), whereby movers select destinations with climates similar to their place of origin. Second, we analyze historical flows of German, Norwegian, and domestic migrants in the US and document that climate sorting also holds within countries. Third, we exploit variation in the long-run change in average US climate from 1900 to 2019 and find that migration increased more between locations whose climate converged. Fourth, we verify that results are not driven by the persistence of ethnic networks or other confounders, and provide evidence for two complementary mechanisms: climate-specific human capital and climate as amenity. Fifth, we back out the value of climate similarity by: i) exploiting the Homestead Act, a historical policy that changed relative land prices; and, ii) examining the relationship between climate mismatch and mortality. Finally, we project how climate change shapes the geography of US population growth by altering migration patterns, both historically and into the 21st century.
abstract_zh: 本文提出“气候匹配”（climate matching）这一概念，将其作为移民的驱动因素，并得出若干新结论。第一，我们表明，无论是在历史上（1880年）还是近期（2015年），气候都能强有力地预测美国移民的空间分布，迁移者倾向于选择与其原居地气候相似的目的地。第二，我们分析了德国、挪威移民及美国国内迁移者的历史流动数据，证明气候分选在一国之内同样成立。第三，我们利用1900至2019年美国平均气候的长期变化，发现气候趋同的地区之间移民增加得更多。第四，我们验证了结果并非由族裔网络的持续性或其他混杂因素所驱动，并为两种互补机制提供了证据：气候特定的人力资本和作为舒适度的气候。第五，我们通过两种方式推算气候相似性的价值：一是利用《宅地法》这一改变相对土地价格的历史政策；二是考察气候错配与死亡率之间的关系。最后，我们预测气候变化如何通过改变迁移模式，影响美国人口增长的地理格局，既包括历史时期，也延伸至21世纪。

title: Church, State, and Education: School Funding and the Assimilation of Catholic Immigrants in the US
Climate and Prehistoric Migration
abstract: What factors drove human migration before modern states, markets, and borders? We develop a framework of ecological sorting in which climate-specific subsistence knowledge depreciates with ecological distance. To test this, we use ancient DNA identity by descent segments to construct bilateral migration flows across Western Eurasia over the last 10,000 years. We document four main findings. First, migration flows decline with differences in growing degree days, precipitation, and soil characteristics between origins and destinations. Second, the dimensions of climate that bind vary across subsistence systems: farmers exhibit strong thermal and soil matching, while pastoralists match most strongly on precipitation—consistent with differential ecological constraints and limiting factors. Third, periods of warming increase farmer expansion while cooling increases pastoral expansion in patterns that recover known archaeological migration episodes. Migration also acts as a margin of climate adaptation: populations exposed to temperature change move to destinations that partly offset the shift. Fourth, genetic flow predicts subsequent convergence in destination vegetation toward migrants’ ecological profiles, consistent with migration shaping landscape change and the demic diffusion of subsistence practices.
abstract_zh: 在现代国家、市场和边界出现之前，是什么因素驱动了人类迁移？我们提出一个生态分选框架，其中气候特定的生计知识会随生态距离而贬值。为检验这一框架，我们利用古DNA的同源片段（identity by descent segments），构建了过去10000年间西欧亚地区的双边迁移流量。我们得出四项主要发现。第一，迁移流量随起点与终点之间积温、降水量和土壤特征的差异而减少。第二，起约束作用的气候维度因生计体系而异：农民表现出较强的温度和土壤匹配，而牧民则在降水方面匹配度最高，这与不同的生态约束和限制性因素相一致。第三，气候变暖时期促进农民扩张，气候变冷时期促进牧民扩张，这一模式与已知的考古迁移事件相吻合。迁移也是一种气候适应的途径：暴露于温度变化之下的人群会迁往能部分抵消这种变化的目的地。第四，基因流动可预测目的地植被随后向迁移者的生态特征趋同，这与迁移塑造景观变化以及生计实践的扩散式传播相一致。
